first.rationale: Current situation shows simultaneous 6% activation decline and 4% onboarding decline, despite memory_86 confirming shortened onboarding historically lifted adoption. This suggests the decline is not driven by onboarding length but by engagement gaps post-signup. memory_91 directly addresses week-one engagement through in-product activation messaging, which is the most precise lever for the 6% activation drop. While memory_73 flags competitive pricing pressure, premature promotional pricing risks brand positioning and sustainable revenue; referral programs (memory_57) require healthy existing activation to compound effectively. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) doesn't address the SMB self-serve activation leak. Verifying memory_86 and memory_91 will confirm whether shortening onboarding alone is insufficient and whether activation messaging in-product has durable effect. A standard_experiment on activation_messaging targets the measurable activation shortfall with a proven lever, preserves ability to layer other tactics later, and aligns with long-term qualified revenue over short-term share defense.
